title: What if π was exactly 3 for 5 seconds? 🥯 Every circle in the universe loses 4.5% — manhole covers pop into cones, wheels buckle, the Sun turns into a lemon. A flat disc can't lose a 16° slice without becoming a cone. Every rigid wheel suddenly has 4.7% too much rim. Earth's equator would be 1,122 miles too long, so the ground has to fold somewhere. Real story: in 1897, Indiana's House voted 67–0 for a bill implying π = 3.2. The Senate shelved it. Which would break first near you? 👇 #whatif #pov #simulation #science #fyp

title_pattern.notes: Same template as the channel's other outlier (7693305573487562016, 'What if oxygen disappeared for 5 seconds?'). Hook = tiny, absurdly specific change (π 3.14159 -> 3) x tiny duration (5 s) -> universe-scale consequences. The caption doubles as an SEO-rich mini-script with exact numbers (4.5%, 16°, 4.7%, 1,122 miles) and ends with a comment-bait question. On-video title is just the question; the 🥯 emoji ties to the bagel prop held in POV.

thumbnail.composition: Auto cover = an early frame (~0.5 s): first-person POV standing on a Central-Park-style road looking toward a Manhattan skyline; strangers walking away from camera on both lanes; child with a red balloon centre; soap bubbles left; white line circle diagram (radius ticks, 'π = 3.14159265...') floating top-left over the sky; title centred at upper third; HUD ring + countdown at left mid-height; edge of a bagel in the bottom-right corner.
thumbnail.text: 'What if π was exactly 3 / for 5 seconds?' in white thin serif (Cormorant/EB Garamond look), two centred lines, no stroke/box, soft shadow. HUD: 'π BECOMES 3 IN' small caps + '0:08.000' large serif + tiny 'π = 3.14159265...'.
thumbnail.colours: Soft daylight low-poly 3D: pale blue sky, grey-beige skyscrapers, green grass, dark grey asphalt with white lane lines; single saturated accent = red balloon (plus yellow sweater). White UI linework only.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Huge skyline/infinite road vs tiny human-scale round objects (balloon, bubbles, bagel, manhole) - every round thing in frame is a planted prop that will break. The abstract math diagram floats over the real-world scene, contrasting cosmic constant vs everyday walk.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Question + a live countdown promise imminent visible catastrophe in a calm, familiar place ('something is about to happen to all of this'). Clean elegant typography reads as premium/science, not clickbait. The math circle diagram signals 'a physics simulation', and the red balloon gives the eye an anchor.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: (on-screen, no voice) 'What if π was exactly 3 for 5 seconds?' + HUD 'π BECOMES 3 IN 0:07.533' counting down in real time, circle diagram 'π = 3.14159265...'; calm park ambience while the POV walks forward holding a bagel.
hook.verbatim_0_12s: What if π was exactly 3 for 5 seconds? / [countdown hits 0 at ~8.3 s: white flash + bass hit, bagel snaps, birds scatter, HUD flips to 'ROUND THINGS 0.138 s / EVERY DISC IS NOW A CONE / TIME SLOWED DOWN 11×'] / Every circle just lost 4.5 percent.
hook.device: Question title + live countdown timer (ticking-clock suspense) to a guaranteed payoff at ~8 s; Chekhov's props (round objects everywhere: bagel in hand, balloon, bubbles, manhole) set up before the change so the viewer anticipates which will break. The first payoff lands within 9 s, and the 5 s event is stretched to ~54 s via a stated 11x slow-motion clock.

beats.summary: Premise question title + countdown 'π BECOMES 3 IN 0:07.5'. Calm first-person walk through a park road toward the skyline; round props everywhere (bagel in hand, red balloon, bubbles, manhole, umbrellas). Viewer anticipates.

Countdown hits zero: white flash + audio hit. Bagel cracks, birds burst, puffs of dust. HUD switches to an elapsed-time clock ('ROUND THINGS 0.138 s', 'TIME SLOWED DOWN 11×'). Caption: every circle lost 4.5%.
Pan right to the lawn/carousel: flat discs pop into cones (umbrellas, bubbles, frisbees). Diagram re-appears as open circle 'π = 3'.
Back on the road: horse carriage and bikes buckle - 'every wheel has 4.7 percent too much rim'.
HUD chapter 'THINGS THAT TURN'. Fountain basin erupts, manhole covers spring up/dark discs fly - 'manhole covers no longer fit their holes'.
Stone bridge arch buckles/snaps with debris - 'every arch is too long for its gap'.
Clock, carousel, rooftop water-tower turbines stall/shatter - 'nothing that spins can keep spinning'.

HUD 'THE SKY / NO SPHERE LEFT'. Look up: the Sun becomes a lemon/spindle with a glare streak (amber frame, hard cut at 37.2 s); then the Moon as a wedge/lens in blank blue sky (no caption - visual-only beat).
'Your eyes are round too.' A black needle/cone slices down through the frame (vision artifact), skyline smeared - the effect reaches the viewer's body.
Quieter audio. Road ahead, balls become cones on the asphalt - 'nothing on Earth can roll'.

HUD 'THE PLANET / EQUATOR 1,122 MI TOO LONG'. Skyscrapers lean/bend, dust columns; 'Earth's equator is 1,100 miles too long' -> 'Central Park must lose 595 feet' -> 'The ground has to fold somewhere': a brown earth wall rises across the road and swallows people/carriages. Loudest audio.

Flash at 62.2 s: π returns (HUD 'π 3.14159...', 'TIME ELAPSED 5.000 s', closed circle diagram). POV looks down at own feet and cracked bagel; crack-web overlay on lens/ground; 'π is back. The damage stays.' Final hold on the clock, balloon and park visitors amid haze.
Fade to black, ~1.5 s silence (loop/rewatch beat).

Black card restating the question + small-caps true story: 'INDIANA, 1897 · THE HOUSE VOTED 67–0 FOR A BILL IMPLYING π = 3.2 · THE SENATE SHELVED IT'. CTA lives in the description ('Which would break first near you? 👇').

pacing.note_wpm: No narration. 13 short italic serif caption lines (5-8 words, avg ~6.4) after the 8-word title, each held ~3-4 s with ~1-2 s caption-free gaps; ~77 wpm reading rate over 0-72 s (excludes the end card's ~24 words). One new consequence every ~4 s (13 consequences in 53 s of 'slowed' time).
pacing.note_shots: Essentially one continuous simulated POV camera ('single take') with pans/tilts as transitions; ffmpeg scene detection (thr 0.08) found only 3 hard events: 8.0 s flash (π flips), 37.2 s cut from sun close-up, 62.2 s flash (π returns), plus the 73 s end card. Visual 'beat' every ~1-3 s; caption every ~4 s; HUD chapter changes at ~9, 20, 34, 51, 62 s (re-hook every ~11-14 s).
pacing.time_structure: Real-time countdown 8.3 s -> event; 5 s of event stretched to ~54 s (HUD 'TIME SLOWED DOWN 11×', elapsed timer 0.000 -> 5.000 s); 10 s aftermath; 8 s end card.

transcript_source: No speech, no auto-subs. Burned-in captions + HUD read visually from 1 s frame samples (plus 0.5 s spot checks); full timestamped text in research/library/transcripts/7696143265405488416.txt.
techniques_worth_copying: Micro-change x micro-duration premise ('π = 3 for 5 seconds') -> universal consequences; the channel reuses it (oxygen for 5 s), so the series format itself is the hook.

Live countdown HUD in the first 8 s guaranteeing a payoff, then flip to an elapsed timer with 'TIME SLOWED DOWN 11×' - turns a 5 s event into a 54 s story with a visible progress bar (ring) to completion.
Chapter labels in the HUD that escalate in scale: ROUND THINGS -> THINGS THAT TURN -> THE SKY -> THE PLANET (object -> machine -> cosmos -> Earth) - a ladder the viewer can feel climbing.
Each caption is one crisp declarative consequence with an exact number (4.5%, 4.7%, 1,100 miles, 595 feet) - reads as rigorous science.
Chekhov props planted before the change (bagel in hand, red balloon, bubbles, manhole, clock); the hero prop (bagel) returns in the final look-down shot.
Personal re-hook at the midpoint: 'Your eyes are round too.' - the catastrophe reaches the viewer's own body.
Twist ending line 'π is back. The damage stays.' - reversal of the expected reset, leaves dread.
End card with a true historical fact (Indiana pi bill 1897) - shareable trivia payoff that rewards finishing; comment-bait question in the description.
Consistent elegant serif typography + minimal white linework diagrams = premium 'simulation' brand; red balloon as recurring colour accent for eye tracking.
Audio dynamics as structure: quiet countdown, hit on the flip, lull at the midpoint, peak at the climax, silence before the end card.

code_only_remake_needs.summary: Doable in Remotion if the 3D low-poly POV world is replaced by stylised 2.5D/SVG parallax layers; the HUD, diagrams, captions, timers and end card are pure motion graphics and trivially code-native.
code_only_remake_needs.scene: Layered SVG park scene (sky gradient, skyline silhouettes in 3-4 parallax planes, road in perspective with lane lines, lawn, simple flat-shaded people sprites walking away) with a virtual POV camera: forward 'walk' = scale/translate of layers + subtle bob; pans/tilts = layer offsets at different rates. Alternative: three.js via @remotion/three with low-poly primitives (cylinders, cones, boxes) - closer to the reference but heavier on CPU.
code_only_remake_needs.deformations: Parametric morph of every round prop: circle -> cone/lens/lemon (SVG path interpolation or flubber), wheel -> buckled polygon, arch -> snapped segments, sun -> spindle with lens-flare streak, moon -> wedge, ground -> rising folded wall (bezier path animating up), skyscrapers -> leaning trapezoids (skewX with spring).
code_only_remake_needs.fx: White flash frames at state flips, camera shake (noise-based translate/rotate), particle bursts (birds, dust puffs, debris, water splash) via simple canvas/SVG particle system, haze overlay (white gradient opacity rising), crack-web overlay (procedural radial lines) for the aftermath.
code_only_remake_needs.hud: Left-side HUD component: progress ring (SVG stroke-dashoffset), small-caps chapter label, big serif timer (countdown then elapsed with 3 decimals, driven by frame: elapsed = (frame - flipFrame)/fps/11), two tiny sub-lines (metric + 'TIME SLOWED DOWN 11×'). Top diagram: circle with radius ticks that opens into a gap when π = 3 and closes again on return.
code_only_remake_needs.type: Thin elegant serif (e.g. Cormorant Garamond / EB Garamond via Google Fonts) - upright for title/end card, italic for consequence captions, centred at ~67% height, fade in/out ~0.3 s; small caps for footnote.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Ambient pad + one big hit at the flip, risers/rumbles for escalation, quiet lull, final silence. Use a royalty-free or self-generated synth bed (no TTS needed - text-only format). Optional: add Kokoro voiceover variant to test against the text-only original.
code_only_remake_needs.data: Storyboard JSON: [{t, chapter, timer_value, sub_lines, caption, prop_morphs[], camera{pan,tilt,dolly,shake}, fx[]}] at ~4 s per consequence; script needs ~13 one-line consequences with real numbers + 1 true historical footnote.
code_only_remake_needs.risk: The reference's charm is a richly populated 3D world; a flat SVG version must compensate with stronger motion, particles and the HUD to avoid looking static.
